english.title: Knowingly / recklessly make false statement regarding ID document to which the Port Security Regulations 2009 apply
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without lawful authority or reasonable excuse, made a statement, namely **(..SPECIFY STATEMENT..), knowing it to be, or being reckless as to whether it was, false in a material particular, to a

(A)_[constable,]_
(B)_[a port security officer,]_
(C)_[a person acting on behalf of a port security officer,]_
(D)_[a port facility security officer,]_
(E)_[a person acting on behalf of a port facility security officer,]_
(F)_[a security manager,]_
(G)_[a person acting on behalf of a security manager,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY CONSTABLE / OFFICER / MANAGER / PERSON..),

(H)_[for the purposes of, or in connection with, an application, for the issue of an identity document]_
(I)_[in connection with the continued holding, of an identity document which had been issued]_

in accordance with arrangements made in the port security plan for the control of access to a restricted area or controlled building
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 32 of the Port Security Regulations 2009.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
without lawful authority / reasonable excuse
made a statement known to be false / recklessly made a false statement
to a constable / port security officer / port facility security officer / security manager
for the purposes of / in connection with an application for the issue of an identity document, to which the Port Security Regulations 2009 apply OR
in connection with the continued holding of an identity document already issued, to which the Port Security Regulations 2009 apply

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Regulation 36 creates a defence of due diligence in relation to this offence; in any proceedings against any person for an offence under the Regulations it is a defence for that person to show that they took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: Level 5 fine.

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
